The issue #12 synthesis is in [docs/case-studies/issue-12/README.md](docs/case-studies/issue-12/README.md).\n16\t\n17\t## Quick Start\n18\t\n19\t```bash\n20\tcargo run -- chat --prompt \"Hi\"\n21\tcargo run -- chat --prompt \"Write me hello world program in Rust\" --format chat\n22\tcargo run -- chat --prompt \"What is 8% of $50?\"\n23\tcargo run -- chat --prompt \"Посчитай 1000 рублей в долларах\"\n24\tcargo run -- dataset\n25\trust-script scripts/mine-hive-mind-dataset.rs --plan\n26\tcargo run -- serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080\n27\tTELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=123:abc cargo run -- telegram                       # Do not bind-mount the host\n68\t`/var/run/docker.sock`; the image expects its own inner Docker daemon and uses\n69\t`/var/lib/docker` for that daemon's storage.\n70\t\n71\tVerify the container contract and the `start-command` Docker isolation wrapper:\n72\t\n73\t```bash\n74\tdocker run --rm --privileged formal-ai verify-formal-ai-dind\n75\tdocker run --rm --privileged formal-ai bash -lc \\\n76\t  '$ --isolated docker --auto-remove-docker-container -- echo formal-ai-dind-ok'\n77\t```\n78\t\n79\tThe static demo lives in `src/web/index.html`. Serve it from a local web server or GitHub Pages so the WebAssembly worker can be fetched by the browser. The demo starts with a user greeting, renders markdown in messages, previews markdown input, and includes a randomized dialog mode for hello-world prompts across several programming languages. Browser JavaScript dependencies are prebundled with Bun into `src/web/vendor.bundle.js`; run `bun install` once and `bun run build:web` after changing web dependencies. The companion connectivity diagnostics page lives in `src/web/tests/index.html` and is deployed at `/formal-ai/tests/`; it checks direct browser fetches, public knowledge APIs, iframe embeddability, and a configurable local `web-capture` proxy.\n80\t\n81\t### Full-memory export and import\n82\t\n83\tEvery interface produces the same self-contained Links Notation document by default. In the browser, the **Export memory** topbar button writes `formal-ai-memory.lino` as a complete `formal_ai_bundle` — the entire seed (rules, concepts, tools, multilingual responses), UI preferences, environment metadata, and the full append-only event log — so a single click is enough to reconstitute the session. **Import memory** auto-detects bundle vs legacy `demo_memory` files and surfaces migration suggestions when the imported seed version differs from the running app's. The CLI matches:\n84\t\n85\t```bash\n86\tcargo run -- memory export --from memory.lino --path full.lino           # default: full bundle\n87\tcargo run -- memory export --from memory.lino --path events.lino --events-only  # legacy demo_memory\n88\tcargo run -- memory import --path full.lino --into memory.lino           # accepts either format\n89\tcargo run -- bundle export --path bundle.lino --memory memory.lino\n90\tcargo run -- bundle import --path bundle.lino --into memory.lino\n91\t```\n92\t\n93\tThe Rust library re-exports the same helpers — `export_memory_full`, `import_memory_full`, `suggest_memory_migrations`, `BundleInfo`, `ParsedBundle` — so embedders writing their own surface get the same defaults. The prefilled **Report issue** link records the dialog as a single compact `U:`/`A:` code block and points to [`docs/upload-memory.md`](docs/upload-memory.md) for attaching the full memory export (GitHub Gist or `.zip` workflow, plus redaction reminders) instead of repeating those instructions inline.\n94\t\n95\t### Teaching behavior in chat\n96\t\n97\tThe chat surface can explain and modify behavior rules without leaving the dialog. Behavior is surfaced as a series of `When X then Y` (or `When X do Y`) statements grouped by topic, and the same grammar can also update the dialog:\n98\t\n99\t```text\n100\tList behavior rules\n101\tShow behavior rule unknown\n102\tList all facts you know about yourself\n103\tWhen `Какая у тебя модель личности?` then `У меня символьная модель личности.`\n104\tWhen I say `Какая у тебя модель личности?`, answer `У меня символьная модель личности.`\n105\t```\n106\t\n107\t`List behavior rules` shows the current built-in routing rules, grouped by topic (Greetings, Farewells, Identity, Capabilities, Hello-world programs, Unknown fallback) and rendered as `When X then Y` statements. `Show behavior rule unknown` renders one rule as Links Notation with its topic, intent, match condition, response, source, and the canonical `when_then` statement. The `When X then Y` and `When X do Y` forms (and the explicit `When I say ... answer ...` form) record an append-only, dialog-local override, so the same prompt can answer differently in that conversation. The grammar is recognized in English (`When ... then ...`, `When ... do ...`, `If I ask ... reply ...`), Russian (`Когда ... тогда ...`, `Когда ... делай ...`, `Если ... то ...`), Hindi (`जब ... तब ...`, `जब ... तो ...`), and Chinese (`当 ... 时 ...`, `当 ... 则 ...`). Use **Export memory** to preserve that rule message with the session, or **Report issue** when the fact or rule should become part of the built-in seed.\n108\t\n109\t## Telegram Bot\n110\t\n111\tThe `formal-ai telegram` subcommand defaults to long polling and keeps the webhook server available as an opt-in mode. The CLI is configured through [`lino-arguments`](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments) (a clap-compatible derive), so every flag also reads from the matching environment variable and from `.lenv`/`.env` files in the working directory.\n112\t\n113\t### Long polling (default)\n114\t\n115\t```bash\n116\texport TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=123:abc\n117\tcargo run -- telegram                                                   # polling by default\n118\tcargo run -- telegram --mode polling \\\n119\t  --timeout 30 --limit 100 \\\n120\t  --allowed-updates message,edited_message\n121\t```\n122\t\n123\tThe polling client shells out to `curl`, calls Telegram's `getUpdates`, advances the offset after each batch, and replies through `sendMessage` with HTML formatting. The same `FormalAiEngine` used by the library, HTTP API, and web demo is reused, so polling answers match the other surfaces.\n124\t\n125\tThe Docker image uses this polling command as its default `CMD`, so the\n126\tcontainer starts the bot as soon as `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` is set. Commands that\n127\tneed nested containers should run through the bundled `$` wrapper with\n128\t`--isolated docker`; `start-command` records command output and metadata under\n129\t`/tmp/start-command/logs/`. Issue #195 called this `--isolation docker`; the\n130\tcurrent Link Foundation Start CLI documents the flag as `--isolated docker`.\n131\t\n132\t### Webhook (opt-in)\n133\t\n134\t```bash\n135\tcargo run -- telegram --mode webhook --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080\n136\t# or equivalently for backwards compatibility:\n137\tcargo run -- serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080\n138\t\n139\t# Docker override for webhook mode:\n140\tdocker run --rm --privileged -p 8080:8080 \\\n141\t  -e TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=123:abc \\\n142\t  formal-ai formal-ai telegram --mode webhook --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080\n143\t```\n144\t\n145\tExpose the server through HTTPS and register the endpoint with Telegram:\n146\t\n147\t```bash\n148\tcurl -s \"https://api.telegram.org/bot${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}/setWebhook\" \\\n149\t  -d \"url=https://example.com/telegram/webhook\"\n150\t```\n151\t\n152\tThe webhook accepts Telegram `message`, `edited_message`, `channel_post`, and `edited_channel_post` updates. It returns a direct Telegram `sendMessage` response for both private chats and group/channel chat IDs, using Telegram HTML formatting so code blocks survive the chat surface. [2026-05-21T23:22:20.076Z] [INFO]       "content": "# formal-ai\n\nFormal AI is a Rust implementation of a symbolic, deterministic assistant that exposes OpenAI-shaped interfaces without neural-network inference.\n\nThe current implementation covers the surface area requested in issue #1:\n\n- library API for symbolic prompt handling\n- CLI chat command\n- HTTP API server with `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses`\n- Telegram bot CLI with long polling by default and an opt-in webhook server, configured through [`lino-arguments`](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments)\n- human-readable Links Notation knowledge and dataset export through `lino-objects-codec`\n- Docker-in-Docker Telegram bot image based on `konard/box-dind:2.1.1`\n- GitHub Pages markdown chat demo backed by a Rust-generated WebAssembly worker\n\nProject direction is tracked in [VISION.md](VISION.md), [GOALS.md](GOALS.md), and [NON-GOALS.md](NON-GOALS.md). The issue #12 synthesis is in [docs/case-studies/issue-12/README.md](docs/case-studies/issue-12/README.md).\n\n## Quick Start\n\n```bash\ncargo run -- chat --prompt \"Hi\"\ncargo run -- chat --prompt \"Write me hello world program in Rust\" --format chat\ncargo run -- chat --prompt \"What is 8% of $50?\"\ncargo run -- chat --prompt \"Посчитай 1000 рублей в долларах\"\ncargo run -- dataset\nrust-script scripts/mine-hive-mind-dataset.rs --plan\ncargo run -- serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080\nTELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=123:abc cargo run -- telegram                       # long polling (default)\ncargo run -- telegram --mode webhook --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080      # webhook server (opt-in)\nrust-script scripts/download-datasets.rs\nexperiments/verify-hello-world-examples.sh\n```\n\nExample API call:\n\n```bash\ncurl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \\\n  -H 'content-type: application/json' \\\n  -d '{\"model\":\"formal-symbolic-production\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Hi\"}]}'\n```\n\nExample Telegram webhook update:\n\n```bash\ncurl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/telegram/webhook \\\n  -H 'content-type: application/json' \\\n  -d '{\"update_id\":1,\"message\":{\"message_id\":7,\"date\":1,\"chat\":{\"id\":42,\"type\":\"private\"},\"text\":\"Write me hello world program in Rust\"}}'\n```\n\nDocker-in-Docker Telegram bot image:\n\n```bash\ndocker build -t formal-ai .\ndocker run --rm --privileged \\\n  -e TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=123:abc \\\n  -v formal-ai-docker:/var/lib/docker \\\n  formal-ai\n\n# Preferred when Sysbox is available:\ndocker run --rm --runtime=sysbox-runc \\\n  -e TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=123:abc \\\n  -v formal-ai-docker:/var/lib/docker \\\n  formal-ai\n```\n\nThe root image is intentionally the only supported Docker runtime: it inherits\nfrom `konard/box-dind:2.1.1`, starts `/usr/local/bin/dind-entrypoint.sh`, and\ndefaults to `formal-ai telegram --mode polling`. Do not bind-mount the host\n`/var/run/docker.sock`; the image expects its own inner Docker daemon and uses\n`/var/lib/docker` for that daemon's storage.\n\nVerify the container contract and the `start-command` Docker isolation wrapper:\n\n```bash\ndocker run --rm --privileged formal-ai verify-formal-ai-dind\ndocker run --rm --privileged formal-ai bash -lc \\\n  '$ --isolated docker --auto-remove-docker-container -- echo formal-ai-dind-ok'\n```\n\nThe static demo lives in `src/web/index.html`. Serve it from a local web server or GitHub Pages so the WebAssembly worker can be fetched by the browser. The demo starts with a user greeting, renders markdown in messages, previews markdown input, and includes a randomized dialog mode for hello-world prompts across several programming languages. Browser JavaScript dependencies are prebundled with Bun into `src/web/vendor.bundle.js`; run `bun install` once and `bun run build:web` after changing web dependencies. The companion connectivity diagnostics page lives in `src/web/tests/index.html` and is deployed at `/formal-ai/tests/`; it checks direct browser fetches, public knowledge APIs, iframe embeddability, and a configurable local `web-capture` proxy.\n\n### Full-memory export and import\n\nEvery interface produces the same self-contained Links Notation document by default. In the browser, the **Export memory** topbar button writes `formal-ai-memory.lino` as a complete `formal_ai_bundle` — the entire seed (rules, concepts, tools, multilingual responses), UI preferences, environment metadata, and the full append-only event log — so a single click is enough to reconstitute the session. **Import memory** auto-detects bundle vs legacy `demo_memory` files and surfaces migration suggestions when the imported seed version differs from the running app's. The CLI matches:\n\n```bash\ncargo run -- memory export --from memory.lino --path full.lino           # default: full bundle\ncargo run -- memory export --from memory.lino --path events.lino --events-only  # legacy demo_memory\ncargo run -- memory import --path full.lino --into memory.lino           # accepts either format\ncargo run -- bundle export --path bundle.lino --memory memory.lino\ncargo run -- bundle import --path bundle.lino --into memory.lino\n```\n\nThe Rust library re-exports the same helpers — `export_memory_full`, `import_memory_full`, `suggest_memory_migrations`, `BundleInfo`, `ParsedBundle` — so embedders writing their own surface get the same defaults. The prefilled **Report issue** link records the dialog as a single compact `U:`/`A:` code block and points to [`docs/upload-memory.md`](docs/upload-memory.md) for attaching the full memory export (GitHub Gist or `.zip` workflow, plus redaction reminders) instead of repeating those instructions inline.\n\n### Teaching behavior in chat\n\nThe chat surface can explain and modify behavior rules without leaving the dialog. Behavior is surfaced as a series of `When X then Y` (or `When X do Y`) statements grouped by topic, and the same grammar can also update the dialog:\n\n```text\nList behavior rules\nShow behavior rule unknown\nList all facts you know about yourself\nWhen `Какая у тебя модель личности?` then `У меня символьная модель личности.`\nWhen I say `Какая у тебя модель личности?`, answer `У меня символьная модель личности.`\n```\n\n`List behavior rules` shows the current built-in routing rules, grouped by topic (Greetings, Farewells, Identity, Capabilities, Hello-world programs, Unknown fallback) and rendered as `When X then Y` statements. `Show behavior rule unknown` renders one rule as Links Notation with its topic, intent, match condition, response, source, and the canonical `when_then` statement. The `When X then Y` and `When X do Y` forms (and the explicit `When I say ... answer ...` form) record an append-only, dialog-local override, so the same prompt can answer differently in that conversation. The grammar is recognized in English (`When ... then ...`, `When ... do ...`, `If I ask ... reply ...`), Russian (`Когда ... тогда ...`, `Когда ... делай ...`, `Если ... то ...`), Hindi (`जब ... तब ...`, `जब ... तो ...`), and Chinese (`当 ... 时 ...`, `当 ... 则 ...`). Use **Export memory** to preserve that rule message with the session, or **Report issue** when the fact or rule should become part of the built-in seed.\n\n## Telegram Bot\n\nThe `formal-ai telegram` subcommand defaults to long polling and keeps the webhook server available as an opt-in mode. The CLI is configured through [`lino-arguments`](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments) (a clap-compatible derive), so every flag also reads from the matching environment variable and from `.lenv`/`.env` files in the working directory.\n\n### Long polling (default)\n\n```bash\nexport TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=123:abc\ncargo run -- telegram                                                   # polling by default\ncargo run -- telegram --mode polling \\\n  --timeout 30 --limit 100 \\\n  --allowed-updates message,edited_message\n```\n\nThe polling client shells out to `curl`, calls Telegram's `getUpdates`, advances the offset after each batch, and replies through `sendMessage` with HTML formatting. The same `FormalAiEngine` used by the library, HTTP API, and web demo is reused, so polling answers match the other surfaces.\n\nThe Docker image uses this polling command as its default `CMD`, so the\ncontainer starts the bot as soon as `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` is set. Commands that\nneed nested containers should run through the bundled `$` wrapper with\n`--isolated docker`; `start-command` records command output and metadata under\n`/tmp/start-command/logs/`. Vec::with_capacity(block.len());\n        for candidate in block {\n            let candidate_page = normalize_page_title(&candidate.surface);\n            if candidate_page.is_empty() {\n                positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            }\n            let Ok(back_blocks) =\n                target_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&candidate_page, source_lang)\n            else {\n                positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            };\n            // Within-block position: scan each block of the target page\n            // and record the position of the source surface inside the\n            // first block that contains it.\n            let mut within_block_position: Option<usize> = None;\n            for back_block in &back_blocks     within_block_position = Some(pos);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(pos) = within_block_position {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{target_lang}:{candidate_page}#confirms->{source_lang}:{page_title}@{pos}[block{block_idx}]\"\n                ));\n            }\n            positions.push(within_block_position);\n        }\n        block_positions.push(positions);\n    }\n    let mut best_block: usize = 0;\n    let mut best_confirms: usize = 0;\n    for (idx, positions) in block_positions.iter().enumerate() {\n        let confirms = positions.iter().filter(|p| p.is_some()).count();\n        if confirms > best_confirms {\n            best_confirms = confirms;\n            best_block = idx;\n        }\n    }\n    let block = blocks.into_iter().nth(best_block).unwrap_or_default();\n    let positions = block_positions\n        .into_iter()\n        .nth(best_block)\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n    let mut indexed: Vec<(usize, Option<usize>, WiktionaryCandidate)> = block\n        .into_iter()\n        .zip(positions)\n        .enumerate()\n        .map(|(idx, (cand, pos))| (idx, pos, cand))\n        .collect();\n    indexed.sort_by_key(|(idx, pos, _)| {\n        pos.as_ref()\n            .map_or((1usize, 0, *idx), |p| (0usize, *p, *idx))\n    });\n    indexed.into_iter().map(|(_, _, cand)| cand).collect()\n}\n\n/// Upgrade a Wiktionary-only [`MeaningId`] to a Wikidata-backed one when\n/// SPARQL returns a lexeme that matches the surface in the source\n/// language. Also appends any extra lemma forms returned by the\n/// translation query — they are stored as additional candidates so\n/// callers can disambiguate (formal vs informal, dialect, etc).\nfn upgrade_meaning_via_wikidata<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n    candidates: &mut Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>,\n) -> Option<MeaningId> {\n    let wikidata = Wikidata::new(http);\n    let hits = match wikidata.search_lexeme(page_title, source_lang) {\n        Ok(hits) => hits,\n        Err(error) => {\n            provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:search->error({error})\"));\n            return None;\n        }\n    };\n    let first = hits.first()?;\n    provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:lexeme:{}\", first.id));\n    let lemmas = match wikidata.lexeme_translations(&first.id, target_lang) {\n        Ok(rows) => rows,\n        Err(error) => {\n            provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:sparql->error({error})\"));\n            return Some(MeaningId::from_sense(first.id.clone()));\n        }\n    };\n    if !lemmas.is_empty() {\n        provenance.push(format!(\n            \"wikidata:sparql:{}->{} ({} lemmas)\",\n            first.id,\n            target_lang,\n            lemmas.len()\n        ));\n    }\n    for lemma in lemmas            candidates.push(candidate);\n        }\n    }\n    Some(MeaningId::from_sense(first.id.clone()))\n}\n\nfn compositional_candidates(\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    if !source_lang.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"ru\") || !target_lang.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"en\") {\n        return Vec::new();\n    }\n\n    if let Some(surface) = russian_phrase_to_english(page_title) {\n        provenance.push(format!(\"compositional:ru->en:{page_title}\"));\n        return &str) -> Option<&'static str> {\n    match page_title {\n        \"кто ты\" | \"кто ты такой\" | \"кто ты такая\" | \"кто вы\" | \"кто вы такой\" | \"кто вы такая\" => {\n            Some(\"Who are you?\")\n        }\n        \"что это\" | \"что это такое\" => Some(\"What is this?\"),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\nfn russian_word_to_english(word: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {\n    match word {\n        \"доброе\" | \"добрый\" | \"добрая\" | \"добрые\" | \"доброго\" | \"добрую\" | \"добрым\" | \"хорошее\"\n        | \"хороший\" | \"хорошая\" | \"хорошие\" | \"хорошего\" | \"хорошую\" \"яблоках\" => Some(\"apple\"),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\nfn capitalize_ascii_first(surface: &str) -> String {\n    let mut chars = surface.chars();\n    let Some(first) = chars.next() else {\n        return String::new();\n    };\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(surface.len());\n    out.extend(first.to_uppercase());\n    out.extend(chars);\n    out\n}\n\n/// Generate alternate This\n        // covers the politeness variants without changing semantics.\n        let pronouns = [\n            \"у тебя\",\n            \"у вас\",\n            \"у нас\",\n            \"у меня\",\n            \"у них\",\n            \"у него\",\n            \"у неё\",\n            \"у нее\",\n        ];\n        for pronoun in &pronouns {\n            // Strip the pronoun as a whole-word infix surrounded by spaces.\n            let needle = format!(\" {pronoun} \");\n            if let Some(idx) = page_title.find(&needle) {\n                let mut alt = String::with_capacity(page_title.len() - needle.len() + 1);\n                alt.push_str(&page_title[..idx]);\n                alt.push(' ');\n                alt.push_str(&page_title[idx + needle.len()..]);\n                let alt = alt.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(\" \");\n                if !alt.is_empty() && alt != page_title && !variants.contains(&alt) {\n                    variants.push(alt);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    variants\n}\n\n/// Normalize a surface fragment into a Wiktionary page title.\n///\n/// - Trim whitespace.\n/// - [2026-05-21T23:22:49.359Z] [INFO]       "content": "//! File-based cache for raw HTTP responses from Wikipedia / Wikidata /\n//! Wiktionary.\n//!\n//! The cache stores only **source data**, never the logic that computes a\n//! translation. Each entry is the verbatim response body for a URL keyed\n//! by a deterministic 64-bit hash of the URL, and the URL itself lives in\n//! a sibling `.url` file for auditability.\n//!\n//! Why a file cache instead of `OnceLock<HashMap>`:\n//!\n//! 1. Integration tests run with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1` and write cache\n//!    entries to disk. The next time the unit suite runs (offline), those\n//!    entries make the same code paths exercise real wikitext — no\n//!    hardcoded translation pairs, just real cached responses.\n//! 2. The committed cache becomes part of the repo's pre-seed data\n//!    (`data/translation-cache/`) so CI never hits the live network.\n//! 3. The cache is content-addressable and idempotent — running the same\n//!    test twice yields the same files on disk.\n\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse super::http::{HttpClient, HttpError};\n\n/// Default cache directory, relative to the crate root.\npub const DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR: &str = \"data/translation-cache\";\n\n/// HTTP client that consults a file cache before delegating to a real\n/// transport. Cache hits always short-circuit the underlying transport;\n/// cache misses populate the cache after a successful fetch.\npub struct CachedHttpClient<T: HttpClient> {\n    cache_dir: PathBuf,\n    transport: T,\n    /// When `true`, cache misses fall through to the transport. The pipeline\n   *can* parse the Wiktionary translation table for `apple`/`яблоко`\n   correctly — it just had no offline data, so\n   `CachedHttpClient::get` returned a not-found error and the handler\n   formatted the `[en] яблоко` placeholder. The\n   handler defaulted to an empty surface, the pipeline returned an\n   empty candidate list, and the formatter rendered `[ru]`. (Issue\n   #216.)\n3. **Browser offline registry missing the apple noun.**\n   The browser worker carries a small registry as a CORS-safe fallback\n   for the demo. That allowed Hindi and Chinese\n   prompt gaps to remain invisible to CI.\n\n## Fixes\n\n### Rust core\n\n- `src/solver_helpers.rs`: add `extract_unquoted_translation_surface`\n  helper that recovers the surface from English, Russian, Hindi, and\n  Chinese unquoted translation prompts, so every supported language can\n  feed the pipeline without requiring quotation marks.\n- `src/solver_handlers/mod.rs`: wire the new helper as a fallback\n  after `extract_quoted_phrase` in `try_translation`.\n- `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs`: add the `apple`/`яблоко`\n  pairs and Hindi/Chinese targets so the offline cache covers\n  single-noun translation tests across supported languages.\n- `data/translation-cache/`: refresh by running\n  `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1 cargo run --release --example refresh_translation_cache`.\n  The pipeline now resolves both directions to the canonical\n  `wikidata-sense:` meaning id.\n\n### Browser worker\n\n- `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js`: mirror the unquoted surface extractor\n  (`extractUnquotedTranslationSurface`) and wire it into\n  `tryTranslation`.\n- Add an `apple` entry to `TRANSLATION_MEANING_REGISTRY` with\n  English / Russian / Hindi / Chinese aliases (incl. Russian\n  declension forms) so the demo can answer offline without hitting\n  the Wiktionary API.\n\n### Tests\n\n- `tests/unit/specification/translation_via_links.rs`: new tests\n  `issue_216_translate_apple_to_russian_without_quotes`,\n  `issue_217_single_russian_noun_quoted`, and\n  `issue_218_unquoted_russian_translation` keep coverage tight, while\n  all-supported-language cases check English, Russian, Hindi, and\n  Chinese targets plus native Hindi/Chinese prompt forms.\n- `tests/e2e/tests/issue-218.spec.js`: Playwright coverage for the\n  browser worker, including a round-trip (`ru→en→ru`) and native\n  Hindi/Chinese prompt forms.\n- `tests/unit/specification/capabilities.rs`: matrix coverage for\n  every feature capability in every supported language.\n- `tests/e2e/scripts/check-multilingual-intent-coverage.mjs`: CI guard\n  that checks supported-language coverage for tool localization,\n  feature-capability tests, and the browser translation registry.\n\n## Before / After\n\n| Prompt | Before (v0.94.0) | After |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `translate apple to russian` | `[ru]` | `\"яблоко\"` |\n| `переведи «яблоко» на английский` | `\"[en] яблоко\"` | `\"apple\"` |\n| `переведи \"яблоко\" на английский` | `\"[en] яблоко\"` | `\"apple\"` |\n| `translate apple to english` | (empty body) | `\"apple\"` |\n| `apple का हिंदी में अनुवाद करो` | Hindi unknown fallback | `\"सेब\"` |\n| `把 apple 翻译成中文` | Chinese unknown fallback | `\"蘋果\"` / `\"苹果\"` |\n| `Переведи \"доброе яблоко\" на английский.` | `\"[en] доброе яблоко\"` (pre-#210) / `\"good apple\"` (post-#210) | `\"good apple\"` |\n\nRaw CLI reproductions are in `raw-data/repro-before-fix.log` and\n`raw-data/repro-after-fix.log`.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `cargo build --release` — clean.\n- `cargo test --release --test unit translation_via_links` — 9 active\n  tests pass (3 new); pub fn translate(\n        &self,\n        surface: &str,\n        source_lang: &str,\n        target_lang: &str,\n    ) -> Result<Translation, HttpError> {\n        if source_lang == target_lang {\n            return Ok(Translation {\n                source_surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                source_lang: source_lang.to_owned(),\n                target_lang: target_lang.to_owned(),\n                meaning: MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, surface),\n                candidates: vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n                    surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                    qualifier: None,\n                }],\n                provenance: vec![\"identity\".to_owned()],\n            });\n        }\n\n        let mut provenance: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        let page_title = normalize_page_title(surface);\n\n        // Stage 1: formalize — fetch the source-edition Wiktionary page.\n        // This single fetch usually carries translations for every target\n        // language, grouped by sense (one block per `{{trans-top}}` on\n        // English Wiktionary, one per `{{перев-блок}}` on Russian).\n        let source_wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(source_lang, source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&page_title, target_lang) {\n            Ok(found) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{page_title}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                ));\n                if !found.is_empty() {\n                    blocks = found;\n                }\n            }\n            Err(error) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{page_title}#translations->error({error})\",\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1a: many high-traffic pages keep translations on a\n        // `/translations` subpage (`{{see translation subpage|...}}`).\n        // Try that subpage when the main {\n                Ok(found) if !found.is_empty() => {\n                    provenance.push(format!(\n                        \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{subpage}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                    ));\n                    blocks = found;\n                }\n                Ok(_) => {}\n                Err(error) => {\n                    provenance.push(format!(\n The target page lists\n        // the source language under its own translation block — useful\n        // when the source edition is sparse (common for ru → en).\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            if let Some(reverse) = reverse_lookup(\n                self.http,\n                surface,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n            ) {\n                blocks = reverse;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1d: phrasal-variant fallback. Some natural phrases don't\n        // have their own Wiktionary entry (e.g. ru:\"как у тебя дела\") but\n        // a shorter canonical form does (ru:\"как дела\"). Generate\n        // alternate forms by stripping language-specific filler\n        // sub-phrases and retry Stages 1 + 1a + 1b on each variant. Stop\n        // at the first variant that produces at least one block.\n        let mut active_page_title = page_title.clone();\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            for variant in phrasal_variants(&page_title, source_lang) {\n                provenance.push(format!(\"wiktionary:{source_lang}:variant->{variant}\"));\n                match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&variant, target_lang) {\n                    Ok(found) if !found.is_empty() => {\n                        provenance.push(format!(\n                            \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{variant}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                        ));\n                        blocks = found;\n                        active_page_title.clone_from(&variant);\n                        meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &variant);\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    Ok(_) => {}\n                    Err(error) => {\n                        provenance.push(format!(\n                            \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{variant}#translations->error({error})\"\n                        ));\n                    }\n                }\n                if let Some(reverse) = reverse_lookup(\n                    self.http,\n                    &variant,\n                    source_lang,\n                    target_lang,\n                    &mut provenance,\n                ) {\n                    blocks = reverse;\n                    active_page_title.clone_from(&variant);\n                    meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &variant);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1c: pick the most likely sense block when the source word\n        // is polysemous (multiple blocks). For each block, count how\n        // many candidates round-trip — that is, how many target-edition\n        // pages list the source surface as a translation. Failures here do not block\n        // the translation.\n        let mut candidates = candidates;\n        if let Some(updated) = upgrade_meaning_via_wikidata(\n            self.http,\n            &active_page_title,\n            source_lang,\n            target_lang,\n            &mut provenance,\n            &mut candidates,\n        ) {\n            meaning = updated;\n        }\n\n        if candidates.is_empty() {\n            candidates = compositional_candidates(\n                &active_page_title,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(Translation {\n            source_surface: surface.to_owned(),\n            source_lang: source_lang.to_owned(),\n            target_lang: target_lang.to_owned(),\n            meaning,\n            candidates,\n            provenance,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// Try the target-edition Wiktionary in reverse. We open the page that\n/// is most likely to *exist* on the target edition for the source word.\n/// Russian Wiktionary, for instance, hosts pages for Russian words and\n/// records their translations into other languages under\n/// `=== Перевод ===`.\nfn reverse_lookup<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    surface: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n) -> Option<Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>>> {\n    let page_title = normalize_page_title(surface);\n    for edition in [source_lang, target_lang] {\n        let wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(edition, http);\n        match wiktionary.translation_blocks(&page_title, target_lang) {\n            Ok(blocks) if !blocks.is_empty() => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{edition}:{page_title}#reverse->{target_lang}\"\n                ));\n                return Some(blocks);\n            }\n            Ok(_) => {}\n            Err(error) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{edition}:{page_title}#reverse->error({error})\"\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Pick the best sense block from `blocks` by round-trip confirmation rate.\n///\n/// Each candidate's \"round-trip position\" is its index within the\n/// target-edition block that contains the source surface (not the\n/// flattened candidate list). Lower position = the target considers the\n/// source more primary.\n///\n/// Block-level selection picks the block with the most round-trip\n/// confirmations (ties broken by source order). Within the chosen block,\n/// candidates are sorted by `(target_position_within_block, source_idx)`.\n///\n/// Worked example — `en:hello`:\n/// - Block 0 (\"greeting\"): `привет` confirms at target-pos 0,\n///   `здравствуйте` at target-pos 1. Two confirms.\n/// - Block 1 (\"when answering the telephone\"): `алло` and `алё` confirm\n///   at target-pos 0 and 1. Two confirms.\n/// - Ties go to the earlier source block → block 0. Within block 0,\n///   `привет` (target-pos 0) beats `здравствуйте` (target-pos 1).\nfn select_best_block<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n    blocks: Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>>,\n) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    let target_wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(target_lang, http);\n    let mut block_positions: Vec<Vec<Option<usize>>> = Vec::with_capacity(blocks.len());\n    for (block_idx, block) in blocks.iter().enumerate() {\n        let mut positions: Vec<Option<usize>> = Vec::with_capacity(block.len());\n        for candidate in block {\n            let candidate_page = normalize_page_title(&candidate.surface);\n            if candidate_page.is_empty() {\n                positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            }\n            let Ok(back_blocks) =\n                target_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&candidate_page, source_lang)\n            else {\n                positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            };\n            // Within-block position: scan each block of the target page\n            // and record the position of the source surface inside the\n            // first block that contains it.\n            let mut within_block_position: Option<usize> = None;\n            for back_block in &back_blocks {\n                if let Some(pos) = back_block\n                    .iter()\n                    .position(|row| normalize_page_title(&row.surface) == page_title)\n                {\n                    within_block_position = Some(pos);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(pos) = within_block_position {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{target_lang}:{candidate_page}#confirms->{source_lang}:{page_title}@{pos}[block{block_idx}]\"\n                ));\n            }\n            positions.push(within_block_position);\n        }\n        block_positions.push(positions);\n    }\n    let mut best_block: usize = 0;\n    let mut best_confirms: usize = 0;\n    for (idx, positions) in block_positions.iter().enumerate() {\n        let confirms = positions.iter().filter(|p| p.is_some()).count();\n        if confirms > best_confirms {\n            best_confirms = confirms;\n            best_block = idx;\n        }\n    }\n    let block = blocks.into_iter().nth(best_block).unwrap_or_default();\n    let positions = block_positions\n        .into_iter()\n        .nth(best_block)\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n    let mut indexed: Vec<(usize, Option<usize>, WiktionaryCandidate)> = block\n        .into_iter()\n        .zip(positions)\n        .enumerate()\n        .map(|(idx, (cand, pos))| (idx, pos, cand))\n        .collect();\n    indexed.sort_by_key(|(idx, pos, _)| {\n        pos.as_ref()\n            .map_or((1usize, 0, *idx), |p| (0usize, *p, *idx))\n    });\n    indexed.into_iter().map(|(_, _, cand)| cand).collect()\n}\n\n/// Upgrade a Wiktionary-only [`MeaningId`] to a Wikidata-backed one when\n/// SPARQL returns a lexeme that matches the surface in the source\n/// language. Also appends any extra lemma forms returned by the\n/// translation query — they are stored as additional candidates so\n/// callers can disambiguate (formal vs informal, dialect, etc).\nfn upgrade_meaning_via_wikidata<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n    candidates: &mut Err(error) => {\n            provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:search->error({error})\"));\n            return None;\n        }\n    };\n    let first = hits.first()?;\n    provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:lexeme:{}\", first.id));\n    let lemmas = match wikidata.lexeme_translations(&first.id, target_lang) {\n        Ok(rows) => rows,\n        Err(error) => {\n            provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:sparql->error({error})\"));\n            return Some(MeaningId::from_sense(first.id.clone()));\n        }\n    };\n    if !lemmas.is_empty() {\n            candidates.push(candidate);\n        }\n    }\n    Some(MeaningId::from_sense(first.id.clone()))\n}\n\nfn compositional_candidates(\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n + needle.len();\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(body.len() / 2);\n    let mut iter = body[start..].chars();\n    while let Some(character) = iter.next() {\n        if character == '\\\\' {\n            match iter.next()? {\n                'n' => out.push('\\n'),\n                't' => out.push('\\t'),\n                'r' => out.push('\\r'),\n                '\"' => out.push('\"'),\n                '\\\\' => out.push('\\\\'),\n                '/' => out.push('/'),\n                'u' => {\n                    let mut hex = String::with_capacity(4);\n                    for _ in 0..4 {\n                        hex.push(iter.next()?);\n                    }\n                    let codepoint = u32::from_str_radix(&hex, 16).ok()?;\n                    if (0xD800..=0xDBFF).contains(&codepoint) {\n                        // High surrogate — expect a low surrogate next.\n                        if iter.next() != Some('\\\\') || iter.next() != Some('u') {\n                            return None;\n                        }\n                        let mut low_hex = String::with_capacity(4);\n                        for _ in 0..4 {\n                            low_hex.push(iter.next()?);\n                        }\n                        let low = u32::from_str_radix(&low_hex, 16).ok()?;\n                        let combined = 0x1_0000 + ((codepoint - 0xD800) << 10) + (low - 0xDC00);\n                        out.push(char::from_u32(combined)?);\n                    } else if let Some(character) = char::from_u32(codepoint) {\n                        out.push(character);\n                    }\n                }\n                other => {\n                    out.push('\\\\');\n                    out.push(other);\n                }\n            }\n        } else if character == '\"' {\n            return Some(out);\n        } else {\n            out.push(character);\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Extract translation candidates for `target_lang` from a wikitext blob.\n///\n/// The result is a deduplicated flat list. Use\n/// [`extract_translation_blocks`] when callers need the sense-level\n/// grouping (e.g. for picking between the noun and interjection senses\n/// of \"привет\").\n#[must_use]\npub fn extract_translations(wikitext: &str, target_lang: &str) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    let mut out: Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> = Vec::new();\n    for block in extract_translation_blocks(wikitext, target_lang) {\n        out.extend(block);\n    }\n    deduplicate(out)\n}\n\n/// Extract translation candidates grouped by sense block.\n///\n/// English Wiktionary delimits senses with `{{trans-top|gloss}}` …\n/// `{{trans-bottom}}` template pairs (siblings, not nested). Russian\n/// Wiktionary uses one `{{перев-блок|...}}` template per sense. We treat\n/// each delimiter as one block so polysemous words don't blur their\n/// senses together at the extraction layer.\n#[must_use]\npub fn extract_translation_blocks(\n    wikitext: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n) -> Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>> {\n    let mut blocks: Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>> = Vec::new();\n    let trans_segments = scan_trans_segments(wikitext);\n    if trans_segments.is_empty() {\n        // Pages without any `{{trans-top}}` markers (e.g. minimal entries)\n        // still need extraction — treat the whole document as a single\n        // block.\n        let candidates = deduplicate(extract_t_templates(wikitext, target_lang));\n        if !candidates.is_empty() {\n            blocks.push(candidates);\n        }\n    } else {\n        for segment in trans_segments {\n            let candidates = deduplicate(extract_t_templates(segment, target_lang));\n            if !candidates.is_empty() {\n                blocks.push(candidates);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    for block in scan_templates(wikitext, &[\"перев-блок\", \"перев\"]) {\n        let mut candidates: Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> = Vec::new();\n        for line in block.split('|') {\n            let Some((key, value)) = line.split_once('=') else {\n                continue;\n            };\n            if !lang_matches(key.trim(), target_lang) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            for entry in split_inline_translations(value) {\n                let surface = clean_surface(&entry);\n                if !surface.is_empty() {\n                    candidates.push(WiktionaryCandidate {\n                        surface,\n                        qualifier: None,\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        let candidates = deduplicate(candidates);\n        if !candidates.is_empty() {\n            blocks.push(candidates);\n        }\n    }\n    // Chinese Wiktionary: `{{翻譯-頂}}` … `{{翻譯-底}}` blocks delimit\n    // translation tables. Inside each block, every line takes the form\n    // `*<lang_name>：[[surface]]; [[surface]] …` where `<lang_name>` is\n    // the Chinese name of the language and `：` is the fullwidth colon.\n    for segment in scan_named_segments(wikitext, \"{{翻譯-頂\", \"{{翻譯-底\") {\n        let candidates = deduplicate(extract_chinese_translation_lines(segment, target_lang));\n        if !candidates.is_empty() {\n            blocks.push(candidates);\n        }\n    }\n    blocks\n}\n\n/// Extract translation candidates from `{{t|...}}`-family templates within\n/// `wikitext`. Used per-segment to keep sense blocks distinct.\nfn extract_t_templates(wikitext: &str, target_lang: &str) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    let mut out: Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> = Vec::new();\n    for template in scan_templates(wikitext, &[\"t\", \"t+\", \"t-\", \"tt\", \"tt+\", \"tt-\"]) {\n        let Some((_, args)) = template.split_once('|') else {\n            continue;\n        };\n        let mut parts = args.split('|');\n        let Some(language) = parts.next() else {\n            continue;\n        };\n        if !lang_matches(language.trim(), target_lang) {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let Some(surface_raw) = parts.next() else {\n            continue;\n        };\n        let surface = clean_surface(surface_raw);\n        if surface.is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let qualifier = parse_qualifier_args(parts);\n        out.push(WiktionaryCandidate { surface, qualifier });\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Extract translation candidates from a zh.wiktionary block, where\n/// each line has the form `*<lang_name>：[[surface]]; [[surface]] …` and\n/// `<lang_name>` is the Chinese name of the target language (e.g. 英语 for\n/// English, 俄语 for Russian).\nfn extract_chinese_translation_lines(block: &str, target_lang: &str) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    let mut out: Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> = Vec::new();\n    let target_names = chinese_language_names_for(target_lang);\n    if target_names.is_empty() {\n        return out;\n    }\n    for line in block.lines() {\n        // Lines we care about start with `*` (Wikitext bullet).\n        let trimmed = line.trim_start_matches(|c: char| c == '*' || c.is_whitespace());\n        if trimmed.is_empty() || trimmed == line {\n            // Either empty or no bullet was stripped — not a bullet line.\n            if !line.trim_start().starts_with('*') {\n                continue;\n            }\n        }\n        // Split on the fullwidth colon `：` or the ASCII `:` once.\n        let Some((lang_name_raw, value)) = split_on_colon(trimmed) else {\n            continue;\n        };\n        let lang_name = lang_name_raw.trim();\n        if !target_names.contains(&lang_name) {\n            continue;\n        }\n        for entry in split_inline_translations(value) {\n            let surface = clean_surface(&entry);\n            if !surface.is_empty() {\n                out.push(WiktionaryCandidate {\n                    surface,\n                    qualifier: None,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Split on the first occurrence of `：` (U+FF1A fullwidth colon) or `:`,\n/// preferring the fullwidth variant when both appear.\nfn split_on_colon(input: &str) -> Option<(&str, &str)> {\n    let full = input.find('：');\n    let half = input.find(':');\n    let idx = match (full, half) {\n        (Some(f), Some(h)) => f.min(h),\n        (Some(f), None) => f,\n        (None, Some(h)) => h,\n        (None, None) => return None,\n    };\n    let (left, rest) = input.split_at(idx);\n    // Skip the colon character (variable byte length in UTF-8).\n    let colon_len = rest.chars().next()?.len_utf8();\n    Some((left, &rest[colon_len..]))\n}\n\n/// Map a BCP-47 language tag to one or more Chinese names used by\n/// zh.wiktionary to label translation rows. The list is intentionally\n/// short — we only need the languages exercised by the integration tests\n/// — and uses both Simplified (语) and Traditional (語) variants.\nfn chinese_language_names_for(target_lang: &str) -> Vec<&'static str> {\n    match target_lang.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {\n        \"en\" => vec![\"英语\", \"英語\"],\n        \"ru\" => vec![\"俄语\", \"俄語\"],\n        \"fr\" => vec![\"法语\", \"法語\"],\n        \"de\" => vec![\"德语\", \"德語\"],\n        \"es\" => vec![\"西班牙语\", \"西班牙語\"],\n        \"it\" => vec![\"意大利语\", \"意大利語\"],\n        \"pt\" => vec![\"葡萄牙语\", \"葡萄牙語\"],\n        \"ja\" => vec![\"日语\", \"日語\"],\n        \"ko\" => vec![\"韩语\", \"韓語\"],\n        \"hi\" => vec![\"印地语\", \"印地語\"],\n        \"ar\" => vec![\"阿拉伯语\", \"阿拉伯語\"],\n        \"zh\" | \"cmn\" => vec![\"汉语\", \"漢語\", \"中文\"],\n        _ => Vec::new(),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Scan `wikitext` for segments delimited by `open` … `close` template\n/// markers (matching the *prefix* of the template name to allow optional\n/// arguments). Each segment is the text between an `open` opening and the\n/// next `close` (or the next `open`, whichever comes first).\nfn scan_named_segments<'a>(wikitext: &'a str, open: &str, close: &str) -> Vec<&'a str> {\n    let mut segments: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();\n    let mut cursor = 0usize;\n    while let Some(rel_top) = wikitext[cursor..].find(open) {\n        let top = cursor + rel_top;\n        let after_top = top + open.len();\n        let bottom = wikitext[after_top..].find(close).map(|i| after_top + i);\n        let next_top = wikitext[after_top..].find(open).map(|i| after_top + i);\n        let end = match (bottom, next_top) {\n            (Some(b), Some(n)) => b.min(n),\n            (Some(b), None) => b,\n            (None, Some(n)) => n,\n            (None, None) => wikitext.len(),\n        };\n        segments.push(&wikitext[top..end]);\n        cursor = end;\n    }\n    segments\n}\n\n/// Split `wikitext` into segments delimited by `{{trans-top}}`/`{{trans-bottom}}`\n/// markers. Each segment is the text between a `{{trans-top}}` and the\n/// next `{{trans-bottom}}` (or the next `{{trans-top}}`, whichever comes\n/// first). Text outside such pairs is dropped — it's never a translation\n/// table.\nfn scan_trans_segments(wikitext: &str) -> Vec<&str> {\n    let mut segments: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();\n    let mut cursor = 0usize;\n    while let Some(rel_top) = wikitext[cursor..].find(\"{{trans-top\") {\n        let top = cursor + rel_top;\n        let after_top = top + \"{{trans-top\".len();\n        let bottom = wikitext[after_top..]\n            .find(\"{{trans-bottom\")\n            .map(|i| after_top + i);\n        let next_top = wikitext[after_top..]\n            .find(\"{{trans-top\")\n            .map(|i| after_top + i);\n        let end = match (bottom, next_top) {\n            (Some(b), Some(n)) => b.min(n),\n            (Some(b), None) => b,\n            (None, Some(n)) => n,\n            (None, None) => wikitext.len(),\n        };\n        segments.push(&wikitext[top..end]);\n        cursor = end;\n    }\n    segments\n}\n\n/// Iterate over `{{<name>|...}}` templates whose name appears in `names`.\n/// Returns the inner body (including arguments after the name).\n///\n/// We must descend into templates we *don't* match, because English\n/// Wiktionary nests its translation tables inside `{{multitrans|data=...}}`\n/// wrappers: skipping the outer template body would discard every\n/// `{{t+|ru|...}}` inside.\nfn scan_templates(wikitext: &str, names: &[&str]) -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n    let bytes = wikitext.as_bytes();\n    let mut i = 0usize;\n    while i + 1 < bytes.len() {\n        if bytes[i] == b'{' && bytes[i + 1] == b'{' {\n            let start = i + 2;\n            let mut depth: u32 = 1;\n            let mut j = start;\n            while j + 1 < bytes.len() && depth > 0 {\n                if bytes[j] == b'{' && bytes[j + 1] == b'{' {\n                    depth += 1;\n                    j += 2;\n                } else if bytes[j] == b'}' && bytes[j + 1] == b'}' {\n                    depth -= 1;\n                    if depth == 0 {\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    j += 2;\n                } else {\n                    j += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            if depth != 0 {\n                // Unbalanced wikitext — advance past the opening braces\n                // rather than abandoning the rest of the document.\n                i += 2;\n                continue;\n            }\n            let body = &wikitext[start..j];\n            let name_end = body\n                .find('|')\n                .unwrap_or_else(|| body.find('}').unwrap_or(body.len()));\n            let name = body[..name_end].trim();\n            if names.iter().any(|n| n.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name)) {\n                out.push(body.to_owned());\n                // Skip past this match. Matched templates (`{{t+|ru|…}}`,\n                // `{{перев-блок|…}}`) don't nest within themselves, so\n                // there's no need to descend further.\n                i = j + 2;\n            } else {\n                // Descend into the unmatched template to find nested\n                // candidates such as `{{t+|ru|…}}` inside\n                // `{{multitrans|data=…}}`.\n                i += 2;\n            }\n        } else {\n            i += 1;\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Strip `[[link]]`, `[[alt|display]]`, `{{nested|...}}`, `<ref>...</ref>`\n/// and trailing punctuation from a raw template surface argument.\n#[must_use]\npub fn clean_surface(raw: &str) -> String {\n    // Drop `alt=`, `tr=`, `lit=` etc — they are key=value pairs and not\n    // the surface form. The caller already split on `|`, so this\n    // protects against malformed input where a `=` snuck through.\n    let raw = if let Some((key, value)) = raw.split_once('=') {\n        if !key.contains(' ')\n            && !key.contains('[')\n            && key.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_')\n        {\n            value\n        } else {\n            raw\n        }\n    } else {\n        raw\n    };\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(raw.len());\n    let mut iter = raw.chars().peekable();\n    while let Some(character) = iter.next() {\n        match character {\n            '[' if iter.peek() == Some(&'[') => {\n                iter.next();\n                // Read until \"]]\"\n                let mut inner = String::new();\n                while let Some(c) = iter.next() {\n                    if c == ']' && iter.peek() == Some(&']') {\n                        iter.next();\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    inner.push(c);\n                }\n                // For `[[alt|display]]` keep the display form.\n                let display = inner.rsplit_once('|').map_or(inner.as_str(), |s| s.1);\n                out.push_str(display);\n            }\n            '{' if iter.peek() == Some(&'{') => {\n                iter.next();\n                let mut depth: u32 = 1;\n                while let Some(c) = iter.next() {\n                    if c == '{' && iter.peek() == Some(&'{') {\n                        iter.next();\n                        depth += 1;\n                    } else if c == '}' && iter.peek() == Some(&'}') {\n                        iter.next();\n                        depth -= 1;\n                        if depth == 0 {\n                            break;\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            '<' => {\n                // Skip <ref>...</ref> or stray tags.\n                for c in iter.by_ref() {\n                    if c == '>' {\n                        break;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            _ => out.push(character),\n        }\n    }\n    let trimmed = out.trim().trim_end_matches(',').trim();\n    // Russian Wiktionary lists transliterations in parentheses after the\n    // translation: `[[hello]] (хэлло)`. Strip the trailing parenthetical\n    // so the surface stays a pure lemma. We only strip a *single* trailing\n    // group of balanced parentheses so we do not accidentally remove\n    // parts of e.g. `(?)` glosses inside the lemma.\n    let trimmed = strip_trailing_parenthetical(trimmed);\n    // Russian Wiktionary marks stressed vowels with U+0301 (combining\n    // acute accent) inside translation templates: `{{t+|ru|приве́т}}`.\n    // The actual orthographic form does not carry the accent — strip it\n    // so callers see \"привет\" rather than \"приве́т\".\n    strip_combining_accents(&trimmed)\n}\n\n/// Strip a single trailing `(...)` group from `input`, but only when the\n/// parenthetical sits at the very end and contains balanced parentheses.\nfn strip_trailing_parenthetical(input: &str) -> String {\n    let bytes = input.as_bytes();\n    if bytes.last() != Some(&b')') {\n        return input.to_owned();\n    }\n    let mut depth: i32 = 0;\n    let mut open_at: Option<usize> = None;\n    for (idx, ch) in input.char_indices().rev() {\n        match ch {\n            ')' => depth += 1,\n            '(' => {\n                depth -= 1;\n                if depth == 0 {\n                    open_at = Some(idx);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n    let Some(open) = open_at else {\n        return input.to_owned();\n    };\n    let prefix = input[..open].trim_end();\n    if prefix.is_empty() {\n        input.to_owned()\n    } else {\n        prefix.to_owned()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Remove combining acute / grave accents that Wiktionary uses to mark\n/// stress in Cyrillic translation candidates. Other combining marks are\n/// preserved (e.g. Hindi nukta, Vietnamese tone marks on combining forms).\nfn strip_combining_accents(input: &str) -> String {\n    input\n        .chars()\n        .filter(|c| !matches!(*c, '\\u{0300}' | '\\u{0301}' | '\\u{0304}' | '\\u{0306}'))\n        .collect()\n}\n\nfn split_inline_translations(value: &str) -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut depth: u32 = 0;\n    let mut current = String::new();\n    let mut parts: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n    for character in value.chars() {\n        match character {\n            '[' | '{' => {\n                depth += 1;\n                current.push(character);\n            }\n            ']' | '}' => {\n                depth = depth.saturating_sub(1);\n                current.push(character);\n            }\n            // Russian Wiktionary frequently uses terminal punctuation to\n            // separate translation variants, e.g.\n            // `|en=[[how do you do]]? [[hello]], [[good morning]]!`. Treat\n            // any sentence-terminal punctuation at depth 0 as a delimiter\n            // so each `[[...]]` lemma becomes its own candidate.\n            ',' | ';' | '?' | '!' | '.' if depth == 0 => {\n                parts.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));\n            }\n            _ => current.push(character),\n        }\n    }\n    if !current.trim().is_empty() {\n        parts.push(current);\n    }\n    parts.into_iter().map(|p| p.trim().to_owned()).collect()\n}\n\nfn parse_qualifier_args<'a, I: Iterator<Item = &'a str>>(parts: I) -> Option<String> {\n    for part in parts {\n        if let Some((key, value)) = part.split_once('=') {\n            if matches!(key.trim(), \"q\" | \"qual\" | \"qualifier\" | \"n\") {\n                return Some(value.trim().to_owned());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\nfn lang_matches(template_lang: &str, requested: &str) -> bool {\n    if template_lang.eq_ignore_ascii_case(requested) {\n        return true;\n    }\n    // Macro-language fallback: Chinese (zh) ↔ Mandarin (cmn), Norwegian\n    // (no) ↔ Bokmål (nb)/Nynorsk (nn). Wiktionary uses the more specific\n    // tag for translation tables; the request usually uses the macro tag.\n    matches!(\n        (requested, template_lang),\n        (\"zh\", \"cmn\" | \"yue\" | \"wuu\") | (\"no\", \"nb\" | \"nn\")\n    )\n}\n\nfn deduplicate(input: Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    let mut out: Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> = Vec::with_capacity(input.len());\n    for candidate in input {\n        if !out.iter().any(|c| c.surface == candidate.surface) {\n            out.push(candidate);\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Percent-encode a UTF-8 string for safe inclusion in a Wikimedia URL.\n///\n/// Spaces become `_` (Wikimedia convention for page titles), letters and\n/// digits pass through, everything else is `%XX`-encoded.\n#[must_use]\npub fn url_encode(value: &str) -> String {\n    use std::fmt::Write;\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(value.len());\n    for byte in value.bytes() {\n        match byte {\n            b'A'..=b'Z' | b'a'..=b'z' | b'0'..=b'9' | b'-' | b'_' | b'.' | b'~' => {\n                out.push(byte as char);\n            }\n            b' ' => out.push('_'),\n            _ => {\n                let _ = write!(out, \"%{byte:02X}\");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Percent-encode a UTF-8 string for use as a URL **query-string value**.\n///\n/// Unlike [`url_encode`], spaces become `%20` (the RFC 3986 query encoding)\n/// because the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint rejects underscores inside the\n/// `?query=` body — SPARQL keywords like `SELECT` and `WHERE` are\n/// whitespace-separated and breaking them with `_` produces HTTP 400.\n#[must_use]\npub fn query_encode(value: &str) -> String {\n    use std::fmt::Write;\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(value.len());\n    for byte in value.bytes() {\n        match byte {\n            b'A'..=b'Z' | b'a'..=b'z' | b'0'..=b'9' | b'-' | b'_' | b'.' | b'~' => {\n                out.push(byte as char);\n            }\n            _ => {\n                let _ = write!(out, \"%{byte:02X}\");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use [2026-05-21T23:36:54.629Z] [INFO]     "originalFile": "//! Translation pipeline.\n//!\n//! Public entry point: [`TranslationPipeline::translate`].\n//!\n//! ## Stages\n//!\n//! 1. **Formalize** — `formalize(source_surface, source_lang)` projects the\n//!    natural-language surface into a [`MeaningId`] by consulting\n//!    Wiktionary (for the page that defines the lemma) and Wikidata\n//!    (for the language-neutral Q-item or Lexeme sense). The\n//!    [`MeaningId`] is the semantic meta-language identifier; it never\n//!    embeds any single language.\n//!\n//! 2. **Deformalize** — `deformalize(meaning_id, target_lang)` renders a\n//!    surface form in the target language by:\n//!\n//!    a. running a Wikidata SPARQL lexeme-join (P5137) when the meaning\n//!    is backed by a Wikidata lexeme, **or**\n//!\n//!    b. parsing the source-edition Wiktionary translation table for\n//!    the target language code, **or**\n//!\n//!    c. parsing the target-edition Wiktionary's `=== Перевод ===` /\n//!    `===Translations===` block in reverse.\n//!\n//! Each strategy is recorded as a `provenance` entry on\n//! [`Translation`], so the resulting links-notation trace shows\n//! exactly which API responses fed the answer.\n\nuse super::http::{HttpClient, HttpError};\nuse super::meaning::MeaningId;\nuse super::wikidata::Wikidata;\nuse super::wiktionary::{Wiktionary, WiktionaryCandidate};\n\n/// Result of a translation request.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Translation {\n    pub source_surface: String,\n    pub source_lang: String,\n    pub target_lang: String,\n    pub meaning: MeaningId,\n    pub candidates: Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>,\n    pub provenance: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl Translation {\n    /// The best target-language surface form. Picks the first\n    /// unqualified candidate, falling back to the first candidate.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn primary_surface(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        self.candidates\n            .iter()\n            .find(|c| c.qualifier.is_none())\n            .or_else(|| self.candidates.first())\n            .map(|c| c.surface.as_str())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Translation pipeline. Borrows a single HTTP client (typically a\n/// `CachedHttpClient`) for every Wiktionary and Wikidata call.\npub struct TranslationPipeline<'a, T: HttpClient + ?Sized> {\n    http: &'a T,\n}\n\nimpl<'a, T: HttpClient + ?Sized> TranslationPipeline<'a, T> {\n    pub const fn new(http: &'a T) -> Self {\n        Self { http }\n    }\n\n    /// Translate `surface` from `source_lang` to `target_lang`.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(Translation)` even when the candidate list is empty\n    /// — callers can detect translation gaps by inspecting\n    /// [`Translation::candidates`].\n    pub fn translate(\n        &self,\n        surface: &str,\n        source_lang: &str,\n        target_lang: &str,\n    ) -> Result<Translation, HttpError> {\n        if source_lang == target_lang {\n            return Ok(Translation {\n                source_surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                source_lang: source_lang.to_owned(),\n                target_lang: target_lang.to_owned(),\n                meaning: MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, surface),\n                candidates: vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n                    surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                    qualifier: None,\n                }],\n                provenance: vec![\"identity\".to_owned()],\n            });\n        }\n\n        let mut provenance: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        let page_title = normalize_page_title(surface);\n\n        // Stage 1: formalize — fetch the source-edition Wiktionary page.\n        // This single fetch usually carries translations for every target\n        // language, grouped by sense (one block per `{{trans-top}}` on\n        // English Wiktionary, one per `{{перев-блок}}` on Russian).\n        let source_wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(source_lang, self.http);\n        let mut blocks: Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>> = Vec::new();\n        let mut meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &page_title);\n        match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&page_title, target_lang) {\n            Ok(found) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{page_title}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                ));\n                if !found.is_empty() {\n                    blocks = found;\n                }\n            }\n            Err(error) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{page_title}#translations->error({error})\",\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1a: many high-traffic pages keep translations on a\n        // `/translations` subpage (`{{see translation subpage|...}}`).\n        // Try that subpage when the main page yielded nothing.\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            let subpage = format!(\"{page_title}/translations\");\n            match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&subpage, target_lang) {\n                Ok(found) if !found.is_empty() => {\n                    provenance.push(format!(\n                        \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{subpage}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                    ));\n                    blocks = found;\n                }\n                Ok(_) => {}\n                Err(error) => {\n                    provenance.push(format!(\n                        \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{subpage}#translations->error({error})\",\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1b: when the source-edition table came up empty, try the\n        // target-edition Wiktionary in reverse. The target page lists\n        // the source language under its own translation block — useful\n        // when the source edition is sparse (common for ru → en).\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            if let Some(reverse) = reverse_lookup(\n                self.http,\n                surface,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n            ) {\n                blocks = reverse;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1d: phrasal-variant fallback. Some natural phrases don't\n        // have their own Wiktionary entry (e.g. ru:\"как у тебя дела\") but\n        // a shorter canonical form does (ru:\"как дела\"). Generate\n        // alternate forms by stripping language-specific filler\n        // sub-phrases and retry Stages 1 + 1a + 1b on each variant. Stop\n        // at the first variant that produces at least one block.\n        let mut active_page_title = page_title.clone();\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            for variant in phrasal_variants(&page_title, source_lang) {\n                provenance.push(format!(\"wiktionary:{source_lang}:variant->{variant}\"));\n                match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&variant, target_lang) {\n                    Ok(found) if !found.is_empty() => {\n                        provenance.push(format!(\n                            \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{variant}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                        ));\n                        blocks = found;\n                        active_page_title.clone_from(&variant);\n                        meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &variant);\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    Ok(_) => {}\n                    Err(error) => {\n                        provenance.push(format!(\n                            \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{variant}#translations->error({error})\"\n                        ));\n                    }\n                }\n                if let Some(reverse) = reverse_lookup(\n                    self.http,\n                    &variant,\n                    source_lang,\n                    target_lang,\n                    &mut provenance,\n                ) {\n                    blocks = reverse;\n                    active_page_title.clone_from(&variant);\n                    meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &variant);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1c: pick the most likely sense block when the source word\n        // is polysemous (multiple blocks). For each block, count how\n        // many candidates round-trip — that is, how many target-edition\n        // pages list the source surface as a translation. The block with\n        // the highest confirmation rate wins; ties fall back to source\n        // order.\n        let candidates = if blocks.is_empty() {\n            Vec::new()\n        } else {\n            select_best_block(\n                self.http,\n                &active_page_title,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n                blocks,\n            )\n        };\n\n        // Stage 2: pull the Wikidata Q-item / Lexeme sense — even if\n        // we already have a translation surface, we want the trace to\n        // expose the canonical meaning id. Failures here do not block\n        // the translation.\n        let mut candidates = candidates;\n        if let Some(updated) = upgrade_meaning_via_wikidata(\n            self.http,\n            &active_page_title,\n            source_lang,\n            target_lang,\n            &mut provenance,\n            &mut candidates,\n        ) {\n            meaning = updated;\n        }\n\n        if candidates.is_empty() {\n            candidates = compositional_candidates(\n                &active_page_title,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(Translation {\n            source_surface: surface.to_owned(),\n            source_lang: source_lang.to_owned(),\n            target_lang: target_lang.to_owned(),\n            meaning,\n            candidates,\n            provenance,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// Try the target-edition Wiktionary in reverse. We open the page that\n/// is most likely to *exist* on the target edition for the source word.\n/// Russian Wiktionary, for instance, hosts pages for Russian words and\n/// records their translations into other languages under\n/// `=== Перевод ===`.\nfn reverse_lookup<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    surface: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n) -> Option<Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>>> {\n    let page_title = normalize_page_title(surface);\n    for edition in [source_lang, target_lang] {\n        let wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(edition, http);\n        match wiktionary.translation_blocks(&page_title, target_lang) {\n            Ok(blocks) if !blocks.is_empty() => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{edition}:{page_title}#reverse->{target_lang}\"\n                ));\n                return Some(blocks);\n            }\n            Ok(_) => {}\n            Err(error) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{edition}:{page_title}#reverse->error({error})\"\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Pick the best sense block from `blocks` by round-trip confirmation rate.\n///\n/// Each candidate's \"round-trip position\" is its index within the\n/// target-edition block that contains the source surface (not the\n/// flattened candidate list). Lower position = the target considers the\n/// source more primary.\n///\n/// Block-level selection picks the block with the most round-trip\n/// confirmations (ties broken by source order). Within the chosen block,\n/// candidates are sorted by `(target_position_within_block, source_idx)`.\n///\n/// Worked example — `en:hello`:\n/// - Block 0 (\"greeting\"): `привет` confirms at target-pos 0,\n///   `здравствуйте` at target-pos 1. Two confirms.\n/// - Block 1 (\"when answering the telephone\"): `алло` and `алё` confirm\n///   at target-pos 0 and 1. Two confirms.\n/// - Ties go to the earlier source block → block 0. Within block 0,\n///   `привет` (target-pos 0) beats `здравствуйте` (target-pos 1).\nfn select_best_block<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n    blocks: Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>>,\n) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    let target_wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(target_lang, http);\n    let mut block_positions: Vec<Vec<Option<usize>>> = Vec::with_capacity(blocks.len());\n    for (block_idx, block) in blocks.iter().enumerate() {\n        let mut positions: Vec<Option<usize>> = Vec::with_capacity(block.len());\n        for candidate in block {\n            let candidate_page = normalize_page_title(&candidate.surface);\n            if candidate_page.is_empty() {\n                positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            }\n            let Ok(back_blocks) =\n                target_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&candidate_page, source_lang)\n            else {\n                positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            };\n            // Within-block position: scan each block of the target page\n            // and record the position of the source surface inside the\n            // first block that contains it.\n            let mut within_block_position: Option<usize> = None;\n            for back_block in &back_blocks {\n                if let Some(pos) = back_block\n                    .iter()\n                    .position(|row| normalize_page_title(&row.surface) == page_title)\n                {\n                    within_block_position = Some(pos);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(pos) = within_block_position {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{target_lang}:{candidate_page}#confirms->{source_lang}:{page_title}@{pos}[block{block_idx}]\"\n                ));\n            }\n            positions.push(within_block_position);\n        }\n        block_positions.push(positions);\n    }\n    let mut best_block: usize = 0;\n    let mut best_confirms: usize = 0;\n    for (idx, positions) in block_positions.iter().enumerate() {\n        let confirms = positions.iter().filter(|p| p.is_some()).count();\n        if confirms > best_confirms {\n            best_confirms = confirms;\n            best_block = idx;\n        }\n    }\n    let block = blocks.into_iter().nth(best_block).unwrap_or_default();\n    let positions = block_positions\n        .into_iter()\n        .nth(best_block)\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n    let mut indexed: Vec<(usize, Option<usize>, WiktionaryCandidate)> = block\n        .into_iter()\n        .zip(positions)\n        .enumerate()\n        .map(|(idx, (cand, pos))| (idx, pos, cand))\n        .collect();\n    indexed.sort_by_key(|(idx, pos, _)| {\n        pos.as_ref()\n            .map_or((1usize, 0, *idx), |p| (0usize, *p, *idx))\n    });\n    indexed.into_iter().map(|(_, _, cand)| cand).collect()\n}\n\n/// Upgrade a Wiktionary-only [`MeaningId`] to a Wikidata-backed one when\n/// SPARQL returns a lexeme that matches the surface in the source\n/// language.
